title: 20.10 A 200GHz 200-Pixel 2D Near-Field Imager for Biomedical Applications
problem: Near-field mmWave/THz imaging systems face challenges: (1) single-source/single-detector-per-pixel limits resolution scalability, (2) lack of proper isolated resonator selection methods, (3) poor resonator Q at high frequencies near lossy biological samples, limiting sensitivity.
motivation: Sub-wavelength near-field imaging enables high-resolution biomedical applications (intraoperative imaging, cell proliferation monitoring) but requires new architectures to overcome diffraction-limited far-field approaches.
method: A 200GHz 200-pixel 2D near-field imager uses four key techniques: (1) Q-boosted Active Split-Ring Resonators (ASRR) enable dense pixel integration with individual selection via minimal capacitive loading, (2) selective pixel activation using shared source/detector (not per-pixel), (3) phase detection replaces power/frequency detection to avoid high free-running VCO phase noise, (4) correlated-doubling sampling (CDS) suppresses low-frequency noise.
key_novelty: Q-boosted ASRR + phase detection enables true 2D scalable near-field imagers with high sensitivity despite lossy biological samples.
contributions: Q-boosted active split-ring resonators for dense 2D pixel arrays
Single shared source/detector with selective pixel activation
Phase detection method robust to free-running oscillator noise
Correlated-doubling sampling for low-frequency noise suppression
200-pixel 2D imager at 200GHz for cellular-scale biomedical imaging
primary_theme: Scalable THz near-field imager with Q-boosted resonators
